title: Donât Put Yourself a Box
description:
Photo by Piotr MusioÅ / Unsplash

Donât Put Yourself in a Box

Personal Development and Career Growth

  • Apr 26, 2024

Summary

  • Companies need "boxes" (job classifications) to grow and function. This makes hiring, compensation, and career development tractable, and promotes fair treatment of employees.
  • If the boxes are too large, a company can't grow. If the boxes are too small, innovation and ownership are smothered.
  • The size of a company's boxes is directly proportional to the level of trust employees have for management.
  • To get hired, put yourself in the box the company is hiring for. Tailor your resume to highlight those skills and experiences; put yourself out there as a âspecialistâ in the thing theyâre hiring for.
  • If aiming for a promotion, demonstrate how your work embodies the behaviors and impacts of the next-level âboxâ.
  • Don't let those boxes define you. Your value and identity goes far beyond any job description.

Hot Take

Businesses can't function at scale unless they put people in standardized "boxes"; if you want to be hired and to grow your career, you need to understand that, and understand how to work with those boxes. On the other hand, you can't be reduced to a box, and if you tie your identity to those boxes in your thinking, you'll limit yourself in ways that are unnatural and harmful.

This is like the paradox of SchrÃ¶dinger's Cat, both alive and dead at the same time. Like with quantum mechanics and the cat, whether youâre in a box or not depends on whoâs doing the measuring: your employer, or you.

My Box Origin Story

My introduction to the idea of âboxesâ came in the late 2000s, when I noticed that people at Google were having a hard time getting hired or promoted if they were doing âoperationalâ work that didnât involve much traditional program management. Whether they were being considered for hiring or promotion, they were told, essentially, âYouâve done some great work, but itâs not program management; weâre not sure what role/ladder is a fit for you, but itâs not this one. Next!â

This was clearly a problemâeven though they didnât do PERT diagrams and Gantt charts, Googlers did important work in these roles, and roadblocks to hiring and promoting them created both operational and retention issues as jobs went vacant and high-performing employees felt their value wasnât being recognized. As a member of both Program Management hiring and promotion committees at Google I had more visibility to this issue than most others; I spoke to a friend of mine in People Operations (Googleâs HR), who turned out to already be well aware of this problem from repeatedly dealing with upset hiring managers and frustrated promotion candidates. Together, we hatched a plan: to create a new job ladder (job classification) for these âoperationalâ program managers to move to, that was better suited to the type of work they did.

We gathered some data, wrote a proposal, and set up a meeting with the SVP responsible for all engineering at Google. The SVP had been in quite a few meetings Iâd presented to before; I knew him to be not only a brilliant and capable leader, but a genuinely nice guy, too, so I had no worries about the meeting. Imagine my shock then, when this âgenuinely nice guyâ started yelling at us, telling my partner and I that we were going to wreck Google culture!

I vividly remember what he said: âDONâT PUT PEOPLE IN BOXES!â He told us Google needed some job classifications, but that our culture required those classifications to be both broad and vague so both employees and their managers wouldnât be blocked from doing whatever needed to be done. The worst thing we could do, the SVP told us, was to make the classification âboxesâ so small people could say âthatâs not my jobââwhich is precisely what he saw us proposing to do!

A year or two before this Google had shifted from having just three job types (over-broadly, they were âengineersâ, âtechnical people that donât do engineeringâ, and âeveryone elseâ) to having around around a dozen (one of which was my ladder, âTechnical Program Managersâ). There had been a lot of debate about whether those boxes were already too smallâ¦ but the senior team had decided 12â15 job categories were acceptableâenough large boxes to make hiring, career development, and compensation more efficient, but not so many that jobs were defined too narrowly. We left his office dejected, but also enlightened: it said a lot to me that this SVP thought it so important to Googleâs culture, a lesson Iâve never forgotten. (Times have changed though; Google now has many more job ladders, including at least 5â10 âoperationalâ ladders broken off from Program Management well beyond what my friend and I had proposed).

Why Companies Need Boxes

Why do we need âboxesâ (job classifications) at all? Wouldnât the world be better if everyone just did whatever they saw that needed doing? The value of boxes to corporations comes down to two things: scaling and trust.

Scaling

If youâre in a small startup, you want employees who can wear many hats, and who wonât feel limited by things like job titles. Because there are so few employees, and because you know everyone personally and need everyone you hire to have an outsized impact, you can afford to put a lot of energy into every individual hiring decision. Compensation planning is pretty lightweight and customized, both because there arenât many people to deal with, and because you want to compensate people based on their contribution to the business, regardless of what their title is. Everyone is a âspecial snowflakeâ.

That changes quickly as your startup growsâyou cross a line where it becomes infeasible to treat every hire as a unique individual, with bespoke hiring and compensation. This is where âboxesâ become necessary: you have to put people into categories, with standards for how hiring, compensation, and career progression work for each boxâitâs the only way you can scale the company. The alternative to this would be to allow an increasing number of managers to continue bespoke hiring and comp within their own areasâ¦ which leads to the second issue, trust.

Trust

Because startups are so risky, the ability of potential employees to trust the founders is a big dealâif they donât appear trustworthy, theyâre not going to attract the kind of people they need. As the company grows, the number of managers that both employees and senior management need to trust grows, too. At some point it becomes too much: employeesâ willingness to âhave faithâ that managers will make fair and appropriate decisions drops lower and lower, so much so that everything will fall apart without the enforced fairness of standardized boxes.

ð¡

The size of the boxes in a company are directly proportional to the amount of trust employees have in management

Labor unions are the endgame for this sort of trust problem. One of the big rallying points for companies trying to avoid unionization is always to try to convince employees that management has their best interests at heart, and can be trusted. As a rule, unions have close to zero trust for management, andâas a direct consequenceâunions often push for the smallest âboxesâ possible: boxes for very narrow roles, subdivided by seniority, and sometimes further subdivided by location. They see this as the best way to ensure fairness in an environment where management canât be trusted at all. This is the ultimate version of the cultural harm my SVP was worried about.

Boxes and Hiring

Scaling and trust drive companies to put employees into standard categories, or boxes. How do those boxes affect hiring, and, understanding this, how can you better âsellâ yourself as a candidate for jobs?

Most companies above startup size need to hire for boxes, for the reasons given above; itâs just too much work to do anything else. It would be wonderful if recruiters, interviewers, and hiring managers had the time to carefully read and savor every resume that came in, and then spend time meeting with every candidate to pull out nuances that didnât come across clearly in their job histories. Thatâs not the world we live in, though; there are too many candidates to get through, and too few hours in the day.

The usual practice is for recruiters to work with hiring managers to identify standard requirements (boxes, again!) that can be used to screen out people and reduce the number of candidates they need to go into more depth with (hiring managers will usually never see any of those dropped candidates). Those standard requirements are typically based on a template used for all jobs of the same ladder and level, extended with custom specs tailored to the particular role being hired for. In the language Iâve been using in this article, the job requirements are a very clear âboxâ, and the screening process only lets through candidates whose âshapesâ fit that box, like a childâs sorting toy.

Source: Flickr user rosipaw, CC BY-NC-SA 2.0

When there are lots of candidates for a tiny number of jobs, the recruiters donât magically get more time to handle the extra candidatesâinstead, they often deal with the overload by tightening the screening criteria even further: that is, by making the boxes smaller.

Behaviorally, the shift from âstartupâ to âbig companyâ, and the shift from rapid growth to slow growth, show up to candidates as employers become increasingly selective. Startups like generalists; big companies like specialists. If there are few people vying for each job, hiring managers won't care as much about past experience; if there are many candidates, theyâll only be interested in people whoâve previously done the same kind job theyâre hiring for. These trends are amplified when business is tough and hiring budgets are thin: hiring managers become nervous about using their scarce headcount on unproven candidatesâthey need people who have already shown success in exactly the job the manager needs done.

ð¡

Iâm writing this in April, 2024, in a time of high interest rates and widespread layoffs in tech, and when there are lots of AI-based screening tools being offered that promise to save recruiters time; you do the math about the current hiring marketâ¦

Besides being lucky, there are two powerful ways to cut through âsmall box screeningâ:

  • Put yourself in the box theyâre hiring for. This means customizing your resume for each job you apply for, or at least for each type of job youâre going after. If theyâre hiring for someone with experience doing X, focus your resume on how youâve been successful doing X (or at least, things like X) in the past. When a recruiter or hiring manager looks at your resume, you want them to jump out of their chair and exclaim: âwow, this person is exactly what weâve been looking for!â
  • Pull a Kobayashi Maru by bypassing the whole screening process: use your network of personal connections to get an introduction to the hiring manager. This is probably the single most powerful thing you can do because it exposes you to the hiring manager as a whole person, instead of a peg that fits in a box.

Boxes and Promotions

A similar situation arises with promotions: the people making decisions about whether you should be promoted or not donât (usually) have the familiarity with you, or the time, to make a customized decisionâ¦ and doing so would create fairness issues. Instead, they look at whether you fit the next-level box. I want to talk about two parts to this: one related to the job ladder, and one related to the level.

Job Ladder

I vividly remember one promotion committee I served on, where we were deciding whether or not to promote an individual who had unquestionably performed at the next levelâ¦ but the work theyâd done wasnât consistent with the job ladder (work classification) they were assigned to. They had delivered amazing business impact through striking personal initiative, leadership, and hard workâ¦ but what theyâd done had nothing in common with the sort of work expected for the job ladder, or âboxâ, they were in. Should we promote them, or not? We debated the question for far longer than weâd spent on any other candidate weâd reviewed, called in HR support to advise us, andâ¦ we couldnât decide. The rules were that âif you canât decide, the decision needs to be ânoââ, so we ended by turning down the promotion and recommending the person for a large cash bonus, instead. Our decision was appealed, and the appeal was denied, too, for the same reason: despite the great work, the candidateâs work was outside the box.

Sometimes the process and people deciding on your promotions will be more amenable to âoutside the boxâ work, but really, regardless of whoâs making the promotion decision, and what their ârules of engagementâ are, your chances of success will be greatly enhanced by you being aware of the box imposed by your job ladder as you go about your work, and as you explain that work to others. To be clear: Iâm not saying to limit what you work onâthatâs the ânot my jobâ problem the SVP at the beginning of the article was talking about! What I am saying is that you should proactively plan how you will describe your work in ways consistent with the box.

For example, if youâre a Program Manager and spent a lot of time creating product requirements (the work of a Product Manager at most companies), when you and your direct manager describe it to others, be sure you both talk about (for example) the work you did to understand what other work was dependent on having the requirements, how you delegated and tracked some of the work on market research, bringing it all together into a single document, how you built consensus on the requirements, communicated them to the engineering team, and then managed scope creepâall things that are part of the description of the Program Management box. This makes it easy for the people who will decide on your promotion to say âHuzzah! They did both the Program and Product Managementâ, instead of saying âThis was great Product Management, too bad theyâre a Program Manager.â

Job Level

Really, this is a topic that deserves (and will get) an article all on its own, but I think itâs relevant to surface it here: in general, higher level jobs arenât just harder/bigger/broader versions of lower level jobs: theyâre different âboxesâ altogether. The next-level behaviors senior people are looking for are often behaviors that arenât exercised much, if at all, at your current level. I think of these as âphase changesâ, analogous to the phase changes water goes through as it turns from solid ice to liquid to gas as you turn up the heat: itâs always the same water, but it looks and behaves differently in each phase. Some of these transitions are more abrupt and noticeable than others, but theyâre definitely there. At Google for example, there are noticeable differences between all levels, but the âphase changesâ are especially acute between levels 5 and 6, and between levels 7 and 8.

The takeaway here is that you can greatly increases your chances of success by understanding what those âphase changesâ are (more senior mentors can be super helpful in this)âwhatâs qualitatively different about the next-level boxâand then work with your manager to proactively plan how you will describe your work in ways that highlight those qualitative differences.

Boxes and You

So after telling you about the importance of âboxesâ, now Iâm going to tell youâ¦ to avoid them!

This sure looks like a paradox, but let me explain!

Weâve been talking about how companies, managers, and recruiters use boxes, and how, because of scaling and trust, itâs just not practical for them to operate in any other way. Weâd hope that they donât make the boxes too small, and that they have good judgment in how they apply themâ¦ but boxes are a fact of life in the world of work.

The place where you should avoid boxes isnât in the workplace, though: it's in your head. Itâs completely natural for peopleâs occupation and organization to become a part of their identityâ¦ but it's harmful to let that go too far: you are not your job, and you are not your job title.

A lot has been written about the psychology of tying oneâs identity to their job, but the thing I want to focus on here is how putting yourself in a box in your own thinking (e.g. seeing yourself as a âProduct Managerâ, as a âGooglerâ, and so on) can mean putting counterproductive limits on your own behavior, and your own thinking about whatâs possible.

ð¡

Youâre much more than, and much more capable than, the box youâre in.

From a career perspective, itâs a good practice to periodically take some time out and take stock of where you are now and how that fits with where you want to go. If you do this sort of self-assessment youâll often decide youâre basically on the right path and just need to make some minor adjustmentsâ¦ but sometimes youâll realize that the path youâre on wonât take you where you want to be, and that bigger changes are needed: maybe you should ask your manager for different responsibilities? Change teams? Change job ladders? Even change companies? All of those require seeing beyond the box youâre in.

Even though you need to describe yourself in terms of boxes to get where you are now, if your own thinking is constrained by those boxes, it will be hard for you to see that maybe the best path for you is quite different from the one youâre on. Maybe you should change teams? Roles? Departments? Even change your city, or your employer? Donât get me wrong: I know plenty of people whoâve been in more or less the same job, in the same place, working for the same company, for many years, and theyâre very happyâ¦ but itâs also common for people stay in the same role because they see that role defining them, instead of just being something they do.

How You Can Bring Order From Chaos, Today

Here are some things you can do now to apply these ideas:

  • If youâre looking for a job now, describe yourself as being well inside the box your potential employer is hiring for: tune your resume to the job youâre going after. You should have a different resume at least for every âclassâ of job, and sometimes for each specific job. It can be hard to do it if youâre going after several types of job at the same time, but your LinkedIn resume needs to support the more focused, specialized resumes youâre using. Make sure you highlight the skills and expertise called out in the job ads youâre applying to, and talk about your skill and experience in that area. No one hires generalists, so donât call yourself one in your resume; instead, describe yourself as a specialist in the very thing your target company is hiring for.
  • If youâre working toward a promotion now, put yourself in the box you want to be promoted to. Ask your manager and mentors to help you understand the heart of the next-level box, and think about how you can describe your work, behavior, and accomplishments in terms of that box.
  • Donât tie your identity to the box youâre in. You are a complete person with a personality, skills, and experience that transcend any mere box, and if you tie up your identity with the boxes other people put you in, you will limit the paths you can take and the things you can accomplish.

What Do You Think?

I'd love to hear about your experiences with boxes! If you're a paid supporter of this newsletter (hint, hint!) you can add comments below.

title: Why do you want this new job
description:
No matter which side of the table youâve sat during interviews, youâve probably heard this question: âWhy do you want this new job?â

In the recent past, Iâve interviewed a few candidates and heard the following answers so far:

  • Iâm not learning much on the current job after itâs been 2-4 years.
  • Iâm looking for something that offers better work-life balance.
  • Iâm not really looking for a job. The recruiters got in touch and I thought Iâd discuss.
  • Iâm looking for more challenging work.

All of the above are valid answers. I think thereâs another perfectly valid answer that candidates seldom mention probably due to the gravity of the interview room situation. Iâve interviewed over a hundred candidates across different companies and am yet to find anyone that mentions: I am not happy with my current salary and benefits compared to my skills

Back to topic of answers. So, when someone answers that they are not learning new things on the job, obviously, youâd be curios to know why and how they have tried to change things. Unfortunately, most candidates simply mention that they are doing repeat work and thereâs not much to learn doing the same thing over and over again. This is where I start feeling a little uneasy. However, I understand that itâs a true statement. If youâre in a similar situation, hereâs some suggestion: read books, and write code based on what youâve read. Then, you can tell a much convincing story that, Iâve forced myself to learn new things and hereâs some proof, but I really want to apply the newly learned skills outside the scope of the âhello worldâ skills.

About work-life balance, I totally hear you. And if your current job doesnât suit what you need out of your life, itâs a perfectly valid reason to look for new opportunities. However, make sure youâre able to clearly set the expectation with your potential employer about what work-life balance means for you. For example, if you canât work over 40 hours a week, or must work from home one-two days a week, itâs best to discuss this even before an interview starts to ensure youâre a good match with the employer.

If you showed up at in interview just because a recruiter got in touch, Iâd say introspect first. Itâs possible that on our subconcious mind you have expectations that the potential of the new job offers you something that you donât get at the current job. So, instead of a passive asnwer that the you simply acted based on the recruiterâs invite, itâs much convincing to see if you can lay down one or two things that you expect from the new job that you donât get at the current job.

About looking for more challenge, it sounds like a cliche unless you can share examples of work that is of challenging to you. May be you like the challenge of using more complicated algorithms, may be you like dealing with a lot of data, may be you like supporting production emergencies, but thereâs gotta be something that you can explicitly mention as challenging. It helps employers to understand if theyâre able to provide you with enough challenge on the job.

Finally, if youâre looking for a new job because the current job isnât paying upto the level of your skills and contributions, make sure to communicate it clearly as well. With salaries and benefits, I find it much easier to work with people that know the actual $ figure thatâll make them happy instead of beating around the bush to create confusions all around. Just be confident and tell what makes you happy. If the employer can afford it, most likely theyâll want to get you onboard as a happy employee. If they canât afford it, theyâll do their best. The key here is to be explicit about what you want and be sure and confident about it.

In a nutshell, when you walk into an interview itâs yours to lose. The potential employer is investing their time and resources and would rather have you hired than having to interview other candidates. As long as you are able to justify why you want the new job, theyâll be quite accommodating.

title: (Senior) Account Manager
description:
Your Impact

We're strong at landing new customers. Now we need to get excellent at growing them.

Expanding within the customer base is one of Tacto's biggest growth levers, and we're building it out for the long term. Most mature B2B companies generate 50%+ of their revenue from existing customers - we want to capture more of that potential, and we're strengthening the team to get there. As Account Manager, you'll be a driving force behind our expansion motion: identifying and closing upsells, cross-sells, and strategic price increases across our customer base, and helping build and sharpen the playbook as we scale it. You'll work between Sales, Customer Value, and Product, spotting growth opportunities and turning them into revenue. This is your chance to build and grow a crucial commercial function at one of Europe's fastest growing industrial AI companies.

Your Tasks

  • Own deals end-to-end: Identify opportunities, build business cases, run negotiations, close deals. Manage contracts and pricing logic.

  • Master account intelligence: Read customer dynamics, map stakeholders, understand politics. Know when to drive expansion yourself vs. when to bring in AEs or Customer Value. Identify perfect timing for upsells.

  • Coordinate across functions: Coordinate with Sales (pipeline), Customer Success (value-delivery), Product (what to sell), and Finance (forecasting) to drive expansion deals

  • Own forecasting and planning: Build accurate expansion forecasts. Coordinate deal timelines. Keep the business informed and on track.

  • Translate roadmap into revenue: Work with Product and Marketing to turn new modules into concrete expansion conversations with the right customers at the right time.

  • Help building the function as it scales: Turn what you learn into reusable process, qualification criteria, pricing guardrails, forecasting templates, rules of engagement with Sales and Customer Value. Where the playbook doesn't exist yet, you help writing it

Your Profile

We're looking for someone who can build, close, and scale. Here's what typically works:

  • 2-4 years in high-performance environments: A proven track record of hitting, and significantly overachieving, quarterly or yearly commercial targets, in account management, sales, or a customer success role with a real commercial component.

  • Proven commercial track record in B2B SaaS companies.

  • Extremely smart and driven – you connect dots quickly, learn fast, and push hard to win

  • Excellent stakeholder management – you navigate complex organizations, build relationships with senior buyers (Heads of Procurement, C-Level), and align internal teams

  • Negotiation toughness – you hold your ground in price discussions without burning bridges

  • Process-oriented – you own details: contracts, terms, renewal dates, forecasting

  • Genuine interest in industrial procurement – you want to understand how manufacturing companies work and speak their language

  • Native German + fluent English

Why This Role is Awesome

This is the first dedicated Account Manager seat at Tacto. Some first structures exist, but most of the function is still yours to build: the quota model, the rules of engagement with Sales and Customer Value, the process itself. Get this right, and expansion becomes Tacto's biggest new revenue lever within two to three years, that's the scale of upside on the table. Do it well for the first 12 to 18 months, and you define your next step: a bigger book of accounts, leading the function as it grows into a full team, or a move into Sales or Customer Value leadership.

What This Role Is - and Isn't

  • This is not customer support with a sales quota bolted on. You'll be measured on revenue, not on being liked, and some weeks that means pushing a commercial conversation the customer wasn't asking for.

  • This is not a mature, handed-to-you playbook. You'll build your own pipeline, your own forecast discipline, and parts of the process itself.

  • Prove you can turn module adoption into signed expansion revenue, and we'll back you owning a bigger book, leading the function, or moving into Sales or CV leadership next.

Why Tacto

  • We bet on young talent and mean it. We consistently back smart, hungry, young people with real ownership early. The large majority of our Leadership Team was promoted internally, you deliver impact and the sky is the limit at Tacto.

  • Backed to win big. We're Sequoia and Index Ventures-funded, with more than €50M raised. We're building Tacto to be the lighthouse for European industrial AI.

  • A truly AI-native organization, with every resource you could dream of. All the leading AI tools and custom agents at your fingertips, plus dedicated people who keep us at the frontier.

  • High bar, high speed, genuinely fun. You'll be surrounded by extremely smart and ambitious people who set the bar high and push you to get better every week. Intense, fast, and the opposite of boring.

  • A front-row seat in the European startup ecosystem. Weekly exposure to leading founders and operators through internal and external events (Lunch & Learns, hackathons, community gatherings). Get a glimpse here: https://luma.com/tacto

  • You'll build something that lasts and that matters. You'll help build the company that keeps European industry competitive for the long term.

Our Background

Tacto is building the intelligence layer that connects AI to the physical world of manufacturing, starting with procurement. AI is transforming every industry, but it stops at the factory gate. The knowledge that holds manufacturing together - part costs, suppliers, materials - is scattered across systems and people. Over 50% of a product's cost originates from suppliers, making procurement the single largest cost lever in manufacturing and the missing connection between the digital and the physical world. Yet it still runs on Excel and legacy systems. We're changing that with our Procurement Intelligence Platform, trusted by hundreds of companies running billions of Euros of material.

Based in Munich, we are 100+ passionate builders who are in-office, with high expectations, fast growth, and a lot of fun. We are supported by >€50m from Sequoia, Index, and Europe's leading tech entrepreneurs and industry veterans.

Why It Matters

Manufacturing forms Europe's economic backbone, driving a fourth of Europe's GDP and providing over 30% of jobs. These hidden champions and global market leaders manufacture the physical world around us, from the machines that build our cities to the medical devices that save lives.

But the world is changing. The US dominates the digital world of bits. China is scaling the world of atoms, manufacturing at unprecedented speed and scale. Geopolitics are more uncertain than ever. Europe's strength lies in its deep industrial knowledge through generations of engineering. Manufacturing worldwide runs on European machines and software. But that heritage is only an advantage if we leverage it in the age of AI.

Tacto builds the AI that connects Atoms and Bits, empowering our Industrial Base to Stay Stronger and building a lighthouse for European tech.

What We Offer

The people at Tacto are passionate about building the organization, growing themselves, and our product while having fun and being real. We have high expectations, great talent density, and a culture where your ambition, performance, and agency are what count - not where you come from or how big your ego is. You'll grow at the forefront of AI, have real ownership and impact, and be surrounded by the best people in their field who challenge you and make you better every day. That is demanding and rewarding, but that's where we thrive. Besides that you have:

  • Money: Competitive salary & equity in the company with real upside, so you are invested in our success

  • Workplace: A vibrant in-office culture (> 4 days/week) in a beautiful office in central Munich

  • Development: A development budget and regular exposure to exceptional people, e.g., Lunch & Learns, peer mentoring, external speakers

  • Time off: 26 + 4 vacation days per year (4 fixed “company rest days”) as well as regular off-sites and team events

  • Health: Wellpass membership, of course, a fruit basket (!), and access to Jobrad, for your health

  • Family & Social Security: Voluntary pension contribution, voluntary KITA subsidy for your children

Tacto is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, or gender identity. Please do not submit personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, trade union membership, data concerning your health, or data concerning your sexual orientation.

title: Consultant Corporate Finance & Unternehmensnachfolge (m/w/d) - Teilzeit
description:
Du verbindest analytische Unternehmensbewertung mit einem klaren Blick für die tatsächliche Finanzierbarkeit?

Genau solche Zusammenhänge wollen wir für Menschen verständlich machen, die eine Unternehmensnachfolge vorbereiten, aber selbst keinen M&A-Hintergrund haben. Dafür baust du das Themenfeld Finanzierung, Unternehmensbewertung und M&A in einem neuen bundesweiten Projekt von Grund auf auf. Gemeinsam mit der Projektleitung entwickelst du die fachliche Ausrichtung und entscheidest, wie aus komplexen wirtschaftlichen Fragen verlässliche Informationsangebote entstehen. Dabei arbeitest du eng mit unserer Fördermittelexpertise zusammen und bringst dein Wissen selbst in Workshops und Veranstaltungen ein.

Worum es dabei geht: Jedes Jahr stehen Zehntausende kleine und mittlere Unternehmen in Deutschland vor der Nachfolgefrage. Bleibt sie ungelöst, verschwinden Betriebe, Arbeitsplätze, Wissen und regionale Wertschöpfung. Wir wollen dazu beitragen, dieses Rückgrat der deutschen Wirtschaft zu erhalten und Betriebe mit verständlichen Informationsangeboten und praxisnahen Veranstaltungen dabei unterstützen, Unternehmensnachfolgen erfolgreich vorzubereiten und umzusetzen. Ein besonderer Schwerpunkt liegt auf Unternehmensnachfolgen durch Mitarbeitende – sogenannten Employee Buyouts (EBO) – sowie auf genossenschaftlichen Beteiligungsmodellen.

Über uns: NDF ist die auf Fördermittel spezialisierte Marke der Key Progress Makers Advisory GmbH. Wir arbeiten vor allem mit Startups und innovativen Unternehmen, die neue Produkte, Technologien oder Geschäftsmodelle entwickeln und dafür passende Finanzierungsmöglichkeiten suchen. Wir helfen ihnen, Förderpotenziale zu erkennen und anspruchsvolle Vorhaben so zu strukturieren, dass aus einer Idee ein tragfähiges Projekt werden kann. Diese Erfahrung bringen wir nun in ein eigenes öffentlich gefördertes Projekt rund um das Thema Unternehmensnachfolge ein.

Rahmenbedingungen: Die Stelle umfasst 19,5 Stunden pro Woche. Die Arbeitszeit kann nach Absprache flexibel verteilt werden. Start ist zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt, idealerweise im September 2026.

Aufgaben

  • Du entwickelst Workshops, Informationsangebote und digitale Orientierungshilfen zu Unternehmensbewertung, Finanzierung und M&A bei Unternehmensnachfolgen
  • Du vermittelst komplexe wirtschaftliche und finanzielle Zusammenhänge selbst in Workshops, Veranstaltungen und Fachformaten
  • Du entwickelst verständliche Fallbeispiele zu Unternehmenswert, Kaufpreis, Kapitalbedarf, Liquidität und wirtschaftlicher Tragfähigkeit
  • Du bereitest typische Bewertungsverfahren, Finanzierungsmodelle, Dealstrukturen und Transaktionsphasen praxisnah auf
  • Du entwickelst Inhalte für die Projektwebsite, die digitale Plattform und weitere öffentlich zugängliche Informationsformate
  • Du arbeitest eng mit der Fachverantwortung für Fördermittel zusammen und zeigst, wie öffentliche und private Finanzierungsbausteine grundsätzlich zusammenspielen können

Qualifikation

  • Mindestens 3 Jahre praktische Erfahrung in M&A, Corporate Finance, Unternehmensfinanzierung, Transaction Advisory oder Unternehmensnachfolge
  • Fundierte Erfahrung mit Unternehmensbewertung und Finanzierungsmodellen
  • Sicherer Umgang mit Jahresabschlüssen, BWA, GuV und Bilanz
  • Ein sehr gutes Verständnis von Kapitalbedarf, Liquidität, Kapitaldienstfähigkeit und wirtschaftlicher Tragfähigkeit
  • Erfahrung mit kleinen und/oder mittleren Unternehmen und ein Gespür für die Besonderheiten inhabergeführter Betriebe
  • Die Fähigkeit, komplexe Bewertungs-, Finanzierungs- und Transaktionsfragen verständlich und praxisnah zu vermitteln
  • Erfahrung in der Konzeption und Durchführung von Workshops, Informationsformaten oder fachlichen Veranstaltungen
  • Sehr gutes Deutsch und eine sichere professionelle Kommunikation
  • Eine strukturierte, sorgfältige und eigenständige Arbeitsweise
  • Einen reflektierten Umgang mit digitalen Analysewerkzeugen, Finanzmodellen und KI

Ein bestimmter Studienabschluss ist für uns nicht entscheidend. Uns interessiert, an welchen Transaktionen, Finanzierungen oder Bewertungsprojekten du bereits gearbeitet hast, welche Verantwortung du dabei selbst übernommen hast und wie du zu belastbaren Ergebnissen gekommen bist. Entscheidend ist für uns außerdem, dass du mit Eigeninitiative und echtem Gestaltungswillen an neue Fragestellungen herangehst.

Passende Erfahrungen kannst du beispielsweise aus M&A, Corporate Finance, Transaction Advisory, einer Bank, Beteiligungsgesellschaft oder Nachfolgeberatung mitbringen. Kenntnisse zu Mitarbeiterübernahmen oder genossenschaftlichen Beteiligungsmodellen sind von Vorteil, aber keine Voraussetzung. Wichtig ist, dass du Annahmen nachvollziehbar dokumentierst, wirtschaftliche Risiken klar benennst und auch anspruchsvolle Finanzthemen so vermittelst, dass sie nicht unnötig abschreckend wirken.

Benefits

  • Die Möglichkeit, von Beginn an ein Projekt aktiv mit aufzubauen und mit viel Gestaltungsspielraum eigene Ideen umzusetzen
  • Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit der Projektleitung und kurze Abstimmungswege
  • Ein interdisziplinäres Team mit Expertise aus Finanzierung, Fördermitteln, Marketing und Veranstaltungsmanagement
  • Mobiles Arbeiten und voraussichtlich 1 bis 2 gemeinsame Bürotage pro Woche in Berlin
  • Gelegentliche bundesweite Reisen für Workshops, Veranstaltungen und Netzwerktreffen
  • Eine Arbeitskultur, in der wir Prioritäten realistisch setzen, Mehrarbeit ausgleichen und Schwierigkeiten früh ansprechen
  • Die Perspektive, auch nach der bewilligten Projektlaufzeit bis zum 30.06.2029 gemeinsam weiterzuarbeiten und zusätzliche fachliche Verantwortung zu übernehmen

Die Rolle passt zu dir, wenn …

… du komplexe wirtschaftliche Zusammenhänge gründlich durchdringst und anschließend so erklärst, dass auch Menschen ohne M&A- oder Finanzierungserfahrung sie verstehen.

… du Freude daran hast, Unternehmen mit deinem Wissen zu tragfähigen Entscheidungen und wirtschaftlichem Erfolg zu verhelfen.

… du dir eine moderne, wertschätzende Zusammenarbeit wünschst und deine fachliche Arbeit gerne für ein Projekt einsetzt, dessen gesellschaftlicher und wirtschaftlicher Nutzen unmittelbar erkennbar ist.

So bewirbst du dich

Schick uns zunächst deinen Lebenslauf. Wenn dein Profil zu uns passt, laden wir dich zu einem ersten Kennenlerngespräch ein. Darauf folgt ein fachlicher Austausch; bei Bedarf ergänzen wir den Prozess um eine kurze und klar abgegrenzte Praxisaufgabe. Nach jedem Schritt erhältst du innerhalb weniger Arbeitstage eine Rückmeldung.

Geplanter Start: zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt, idealerweise im September 2026.

Wir freuen uns über Bewerbungen unabhängig von Geschlecht und geschlechtlicher Identität, ethnischer oder sozialer Herkunft, Nationalität, Religion oder Weltanschauung, Behinderung, Alter oder sexueller Identität. Bei uns übernimmst du keinen bestehenden Fachbereich, sondern baust das Themenfeld Förderung und Finanzierung für Unternehmensnachfolge selbst auf. Gemeinsam mit der Projektleitung entwickelst du die fachliche Ausrichtung und entscheidest, welche Förder- und Finanzierungsfragen wir aufgreifen und wie daraus verlässliche Informationsangebote entstehen. Dabei arbeitest du eng mit unserer Finanz- und M&A-Expertise zusammen und bringst dein Wissen selbst in Workshops und Veranstaltungen ein.

Worum es dabei geht: Jedes Jahr stehen Zehntausende kleine und mittlere Unternehmen in Deutschland vor der Nachfolgefrage. Bleibt sie ungelöst, verschwinden Betriebe, Arbeitsplätze, Wissen und regionale Wertschöpfung. Wir wollen dazu beitragen, dieses Rückgrat der deutschen Wirtschaft zu erhalten und Betriebe mit verständlichen Informationsangeboten und praxisnahen Veranstaltungen dabei unterstützen, Unternehmensnachfolgen erfolgreich vorzubereiten und umzusetzen.

Über uns: NDF ist die auf Fördermittel spezialisierte Marke der Key Progress Makers Advisory GmbH. Wir arbeiten vor allem mit Startups und innovativen Unternehmen, die neue Produkte, Technologien oder Geschäftsmodelle entwickeln und dafür passende Finanzierungsmöglichkeiten suchen. Wir helfen ihnen, Förderpotenziale zu erkennen und anspruchsvolle Vorhaben so zu strukturieren, dass aus einer Idee ein tragfähiges Projekt werden kann. Diese Erfahrung bringen wir nun in ein eigenes öffentlich gefördertes Projekt rund um das Thema Unternehmensnachfolge ein.

Rahmenbedingungen: Die Stelle umfasst 39 Stunden pro Woche. Wir arbeiten hybrid und planen durchschnittlich zwei bis drei gemeinsame Bürotage pro Woche in Berlin. Start ist zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt, idealerweise im September 2026.

Aufgaben

  • Du entwickelst Workshops, Informationsangebote und digitale Orientierungshilfen zu Förderung und Finanzierung bei Unternehmensnachfolgen
  • Du vermittelst komplexe Förder- und Finanzierungsthemen verständlich in Workshops, Veranstaltungen und Fachformaten
  • Du recherchierst und analysierst Zuschüsse, Förderdarlehen, Bürgschaften, Garantien und weitere öffentliche Finanzierungsinstrumente für Unternehmensnachfolgen, Investitionen und betriebliche Transformationen
  • Du entwickelst Inhalte für die Projektwebsite, die digitale Plattform und weitere öffentlich zugängliche Informationsformate
  • Du arbeitest eng mit der Fachverantwortung für Finanzierung und M&A zusammen und zeigst, wie öffentliche und private Finanzierungsbausteine grundsätzlich zusammenspielen können

Qualifikation

  • Mindestens drei Jahre praktische Erfahrung mit Förderprogrammen oder öffentlichen Finanzierungsinstrumenten – beispielsweise in der Beratung, Beantragung, Prüfung, Bewilligung oder Umsetzung
  • Fundiertes betriebswirtschaftliches und finanzielles Verständnis
  • Erfahrung mit Förderangeboten für kleine und mittlere Unternehmen, etwa in den Bereichen Innovation, Digitalisierung, Investitionen, Transformation, Energieeffizienz oder Unternehmensnachfolge
  • Die Fähigkeit, Förderbedingungen eigenständig zu recherchieren, zu prüfen, einzuordnen und komplexe Finanzthemen verständlich und praxisnah zu vermitteln
  • Erfahrung in der Konzeption oder Durchführung von Workshops, Informationsformaten oder fachlichen Veranstaltungen ist von Vorteil, aber keine Voraussetzung
  • Sehr gutes Deutsch und eine sichere professionelle Kommunikation
  • Eine strukturierte, gewissenhafte und eigenständige Arbeitsweise
  • Einen reflektierten Umgang mit digitalen Recherchewerkzeugen, Automatisierung und KI

Ein bestimmter Studienabschluss ist für uns nicht entscheidend. Uns interessiert, mit welchen Förder- und Finanzierungsthemen du bereits gearbeitet hast, welche Verantwortung du dabei selbst übernommen hast und wie du zu belastbaren Ergebnissen gekommen bist. Entscheidend ist für uns außerdem, dass du mit Eigeninitiative und echtem Gestaltungswillen an neue Fragestellungen herangehst.

Passende Erfahrungen kannst du beispielsweise aus einer Förderbank, Bürgschaftsbank, Wirtschaftsförderung, Bank, Beratung oder dem Fördermittelmanagement mitbringen. Wichtig ist nicht, dass du jedes Förderprogramm auswendig kennst. Du solltest wissen, wie du relevante Instrumente findest, ihre Voraussetzungen zuverlässig prüfst und die Ergebnisse für Menschen ohne Fördermittelhintergrund verständlich aufbereitest.

Benefits

  • Die Möglichkeit, ein neues Projekt von Beginn an mitzugestalten und eigene Ideen umzusetzen
  • Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit der Projektleitung und kurze Abstimmungswege
  • Ein interdisziplinäres Team mit Expertise aus den Bereichen Unternehmensnachfolge, Startups und Finanzierung
  • Mobiles Arbeiten mit gemeinsamer Präsenz in Berlin, abgestimmt auf Projektphase und Veranstaltungskalender
  • Gelegentliche bundesweite Reisen sowie einzelne Abendtermine, die frühzeitig geplant und zeitlich ausgeglichen werden
  • Eine Arbeitskultur, in der wir Prioritäten realistisch setzen, Mehrarbeit ausgleichen und Schwierigkeiten früh ansprechen
  • Die Perspektive, auch nach der dreijährigen Projektlaufzeit gemeinsam weiterzuarbeiten und zusätzliche fachliche Verantwortung zu übernehmen

Die Rolle passt zu dir, wenn …

… du komplexe Förder- und Finanzierungsfragen gerne gründlich durchdringst und anschließend so erklärst, dass auch Menschen ohne Finanzhintergrund sie verstehen.

… du Freude daran hast, Unternehmen mit deinem Wissen zu tragfähigen Finanzierungsentscheidungen und wirtschaftlichem Erfolg zu verhelfen.

… du dir eine moderne, wertschätzende Zusammenarbeit wünschst und deine fachliche Arbeit gerne für ein Projekt einsetzt, dessen gesellschaftlicher und wirtschaftlicher Nutzen unmittelbar erkennbar ist.

So bewirbst du dich

Schick uns zunächst deinen Lebenslauf. Wenn dein Profil zu uns passt, laden wir dich zu einem ersten Kennenlerngespräch ein. Darauf folgt ein fachlicher Austausch; bei Bedarf ergänzen wir den Prozess um eine kurze und klar abgegrenzte Praxisaufgabe. Nach jedem Schritt erhältst du innerhalb weniger Arbeitstage eine Rückmeldung.

Geplanter Start: zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt, idealerweise im September 2026.

Wir freuen uns über Bewerbungen unabhängig von Geschlecht und geschlechtlicher Identität, ethnischer oder sozialer Herkunft, Nationalität, Religion oder Weltanschauung, Behinderung, Alter oder sexueller Identität. Entscheidend sind deine Kompetenz, deine Motivation und die Perspektive, die du in das Projekt einbringst.

description:
Mendix – the leading low-code agentic enterprise platform: 

The Mendix Platform uses visual modeling to abstract long-form coding out of agent & application development. Our customers use Mendix to create and deploy better software for the enterprise, faster. Mendix enables collaboration between business users and developers to work together throughout the development process. 

Read our customer stories to learn more about the wealth of software and solutions global organizations have built with the Platform. 

Position Overview

Mendix is the leading low-code agentic enterprise platform. Our customers use Mendix to create and deploy better software for the enterprise, faster. Mendix enables collaboration between business users and developers to work together throughout the development process. Our group is responsible for driving innovation within Mendix as we work on modern technologies crucial to develop and deliver an Agentic Enterprise Platform to our customers. Our local team in Munich develops Agents Kit, the Mendix agent building SDK, so our customers can intuitively develop agents and agentic applications with an engaging end-user experience. You can find most of our components in the Mendix marketplace, and they can be used through Mendix Cloud GenAI Resource Packs.


Key Responsibilities:
  • Build upon an existing foundation, moving at a fast pace as the agentic AI space progresses
  • Work with early adopter customers to build out Agents Kit, an AI portfolio of modules and applications our customers really need
  • Work on a platform with a lasting impact and strategic value, knowing that thousands of developers and millions of end users across the globe rely on your work, and each commit can make a lot of impact
  • Be thorough and get to the bottom of things; clear answers are more important than deadlines
  • Work full-stack across technologies, delivering a Mendix SDK and leveraging TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, CSS, and Java

Qualifications

Required:

  • Mendix skills at the level of an Expert Developer with extensive knowledge of Mendix best practices for development
  • Comfortable writing a Java method or custom widget independently
  • Ability to learn new concepts and pick up new technologies based on tasks at hand, excited by the challenge of sophisticated technical problems
  • Take ownership for the quality of your work and the impact it has on others
  • Familiarity with agile frameworks and software development collaboration tools such as Git
  • Willingness to meet colleagues once or twice a week in a modern office in Munich

Preferred:
  • Background in the domain of generative AI, either through education or work experience in software development
  • Familiarity with technical concepts of MCP and/or A2A and other agent-building capabilities
  • Experience with Agents Kit and the Agent Editor in 11.9+
  • Experience with TypeScript/JavaScript, Python or another programming language
  • Day-to-day experience with agentic development tools such as Claude Code
  • Experience with generative AI services of cloud providers such as AWS, Azure and Google

Why Us

At Siemens Software, flexibility is how we work—hybrid by default, built on trust and autonomy. Together, 30,000 people across more than 200 countries build technology that shapes the real world. You'll grow through real projects, strong technical peers, and global mobility, backed by the scale and benefits of an industrial software leader. We're committed to equality and inclusion, and we hire based on merit, skills, and impact. Bring your curiosity and creativity and help us shape tomorrow!

Our Benefits & Rewards

The salary range for this position is €68,900 to €113,800 and this role is eligible to earn incentive compensation. The actual compensation offered is based on the successful candidate's job-related skills, experience, and relevant education/training. Siemens offers health and wellness benefits to employees; you can access the benefits available in your country via the link: https://jobs.sw.siemens.com/benefits/

Diversity & Inclusion

We value equal opportunities and welcome applications from people with disabilities. At Siemens, we believe people who've had real experiences dealing with being different will excel as leaders. Let's develop a culture of creativity and innovation. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform crucial job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.

As a Full-Stack Engineer (m/f/d), you'll be one of the early full-time engineers, working closely with our senior engineers, Co-Founders and CTO. You'll ship features across the stack — from Spring Boot services to React frontends — and grow into broader ownership as the team and product scale.

  • Shipped meaningful features end to end, from backend APIs to the user-facing React interface
  • Clarified and communicated the core domain model using DDD principles
  • Introduced/standardized an AI-driven development process, from feature specs to production deployment
  • Contributed to a healthy test suite and a reliable CI/CD pipeline
  • Deployed and operated services on Kubernetes, learning our cloud-native infrastructure hands-on

Responsibilities

  • Collaborate with the team to find strong solutions to new types of problems in an AI-first architecture
  • Embrace a DevOps-style approach across the full specification → development → delivery lifecycle (inspired by the DevOps Handbook)
  • Propose and implement approaches to make delivery faster and more reliable (e.g., improving flow, feedback loops, and recovery)
  • Implement and evolve monitoring/observability across systems (metrics, logs, traces, alerting) so we can detect issues early and learn from production
  • Collaborate with the team to develop an AI-driven development process from feature specs down to production deployment
  • Plan & document backend architecture in the Arc42 framework
  • Extend & communicate the domain model using DDD principles
  • Manage and extend application infrastructure on Azure with Pulumi

Requirements

Absolute must-haves

  • You are opinionated and passionate about good code design
  • Solid, hands-on experience with Claude Code (or comparable AI-assisted development workflows)
  • Solid, hands-on experience with Java and Spring Boot
  • Solid, hands-on experience with TypeScript and React
  • SOLID principles & clean code
  • Design patterns

Nice to haves

  • Experience with TDD and/or BDD
  • Working knowledge of Kubernetes and cloud-native application development
  • Azure or AWS infrastructure-as-code (e.g. Pulumi, Terraform, Bicep)
  • C4 modelling & Arc42 framework
  • Experience with Domain Driven Design (DDD)
  • Reliable CI/CD pipelines and release processes
  • Continuous improvement loops (post-incident reviews, operational learning, and prioritizing reliability work)

Benefits

  • Hands-on ownership of a real AI product used by enterprise customers
  • Work directly alongside the founding team from day one
  • Hybrid work model: Munich North, minimum one day per week in the office, otherwise flexible (open to strong candidates elsewhere in the EU for the right fit); onboarding will take place in-office
  • A steep learning curve at the intersection of LLM engineering, enterprise GRC, and startup operations
  • The chance to shape the AI team as we grow

Auxilius .ai is building AI-powered GRC solutions for enterprises. We're early-stage, fast-growing, and backed by real customers. Our tech stack includes Java & Spring Boot, Angular, Kubernetes on Azure, and OpenAI & Anthropic LLMs.

title: Energy Nerd / Developer - Freiburg im Breisgau
description:
“We design the infrastructure systems of tomorrow!” – With you?

We are convinced that the transformation towards sustainable, resilient and efficient infrastructures does not have to be complicated. We provide municipalities, utilities, grid operators and other infrastructure stakeholders with the data, analyses and decision-making tools they need for integrated infrastructure and energy system planning.

To strengthen our team, we are looking for a motivated and solution-oriented Project Engineer (m/f/d) with a focus on heating grids to support the implementation of transformation plans and feasibility studies and to contribute to the development of innovative tools and solutions for future-oriented energy systems.

Tasks

  • Design and develop scalable algorithms for energy system modelling
  • Architect, extend and optimise simulation models in Python, ensuring modularity, performant data structures and reusable code
  • Conduct comprehensive and automated analyses of simulation results to extract actionable insights for energy planning
  • Translate local desktop simulations and algorithms into production-ready software architectures for integration into our SaaS platform
  • Establish and document standardised workflows for data integration, geoprocessing and quality assurance
  • Proactively align on-premise and academic tools with the requirements of production SaaS applications
  • Develop and extend greenventory's internal toolbox for energy system modelling and planning
  • Work closely with energy experts, software developers and researchers to turn complex energy system questions into robust technical solutions
  • Continuously improve the performance, maintainability and usability of our modelling and simulation tools

Requirements

  • You have a deep understanding of energy systems and/or computer science
  • You have strong skills in simulation and programming, particularly Python
  • You have experience with Django or comparable Python-based web frameworks
  • You have 2–5 years of practical experience in energy modelling, data science or engineering software development
  • You have experience with Git-based version control and GitHub, including clean commits, pull requests and branching strategies
  • You are familiar with CI/CD pipelines, automated testing and linting
  • You have experience with QGIS and geospatial data analysis
  • You are familiar with geospatial Python libraries such as GeoPandas, Shapely and PyProj
  • You have experience with agentic coding and AI-supported development workflows, for example LLMs, Copilots or automated coding agents
  • You are familiar with Agile development environments and code review practices
  • You are interested in SaaS applications and enjoy turning technical concepts into production-ready software
  • You have good communication skills in English
  • You can balance the requirements and expectations of an end research institute environment with the practical needs of greenventory and a production software environment

Benefits

  • Career prospects: Work in a sustainable, socially relevant and absolutely future-proof field.
  • Team spirit: Whether in daily work, regular after-work activities or company outings - look forward to a friendly team where you will be fully integrated from the start and enjoy your work.
  • Flexible working: Whether you're an early bird or a night owl, you can arrange your working hours flexibly. In addition, thanks to hybrid working, you also have the option of working from home occasionally.
  • Fair pay: We offer an attractive and competitive salary package.
  • Personal training and development opportunities: We offer you the opportunity to quickly take on responsibility in projects within a strong team and to grow through new and exciting tasks.
  • We work in a state-of-the-art office with top-of-the-line equipment, based in Freiburg.
  • Health is a high priority for us. We therefore support our employees financially with Hansefit memberships and offer the option of leasing a company bike.
  • Work-life balance: In addition to 30 days of annual leave, we also offer the possibility of working part-time: A 4-day week is no problem for us!

"But why exactly Greenventory?"

With us, you have the opportunity to work in an ambitious team on projects that will shape the future. Through your work, you will make a significant contribution to advancing the energy transition and paving the way to climate neutrality.

title: Forward Deployed Engineering Lead
description:
Your Impact

Procurement is over 50% of revenue for industrial companies and their biggest lever for profitability. The hard part is not the software, it is that every single customer's reality is different: a different ERP, a different data model, decades of undocumented process. Generic platforms stall exactly there, and that gap is where most enterprise AI value quietly dies.

Forward Deployed Engineering is how we close it: engineers who sit inside the customer's environment, build in their data, and turn what they learn into product. This function does not exist at Tacto yet. You will build the motion from the start, collaborating with Product, and discover what Forward Deployed Engineering means for Tacto, figuring out how much value we can generate for leading industrials.

Your Tasks

  • Build the function. Charter, operating model, quality bar, metrics. Bring this function to the next level.

  • Hire the right talent. The team is there to grow. Hire exceptional Forward Deployed Engineers and build your own high performing team.

  • Own how we engage customers. Design and establish the processes for how engineers scope, embed, build, and hand over. This is the core of the role, not an afterthought to the technical work.

  • Build, hands-on, in customer environments. Agents, pipelines, custom logic on top of our platform, in real production data. You lead by shipping.

  • Turn one-offs into product. Work directly with Product and Engineering to convert what you build at the edge into platform capability. An FDE org that productises nothing is just an expensive consultancy, and you will make sure we never become one.

  • Lead the first FDEs. Find the rare people who are excellent engineers and credible in front of a Head of IT. Set the standard by being it.

  • Own the hardest customer rooms. Lead escalations with Heads of Procurement and IT and be the senior presence customers trust.

  • Be AI-native. Use AI to change what the function is capable of, then measure it, then build it into how the team works.

Your Profile

  • 5+ years building software close to customers: forward deployed or deployment-style engineering, technical program leadership in a product company, or an engineering-heavy path through top-tier consulting at Manager level or above.

  • You write code and you want to keep writing it. Python and SQL at working level, comfortable with data pipelines and integration architecture.

  • 1+ years leading engineers, or you have built something from zero and had people follow you into it.

  • Zero-to-one operator. You are comfortable when the process does not exist yet, and you write it down instead of holding it in your head.

  • Product instinct. You can tell a one-off from a pattern and you will argue the case either way.

  • Senior presence with customers, including C-level escalations, and the backbone to be clear about what we will and will not commit to.

  • Native or C1 German, fluent English.

Why This Role is Awesome

You are not inheriting a team, you are defining a function that most companies in enterprise AI are only starting to understand they need. Do this well for 12 to 18 months and you own one of Tacto's core technical organisations, with a direct line into the product roadmap and a hand in how leading global industrials adopts AI.

What This Role Is - and Isn't

  • This is not a people-management role with technical decoration. If you want to stop building, this is the wrong job.

  • This is not consulting. Nobody here bills days. You are measured on what customers can do afterwards and on what made it into the platform.

  • The first months will be ambiguous by design: you, a handful of accounts, and a blank page. If that reads as risk rather than opportunity, this is not a good fit.

Why Tacto

  • Backed to win big. We are Sequoia and Index-funded with €50M+ behind us. Our founders sit at the same table as the people defining the global AI agenda. We're building Tacto to be the lighthouse for European industrial AI.

  • A truly AI-native organization, with every resource you could dream of. All the leading AI tools and custom agents at your fingertips, plus dedicated people who keep us at the frontier.

  • High bar, high speed, genuinely fun. You'll be surrounded by extremely smart and ambitious people who set the bar high and push you to get better every week. Intense, fast, and the opposite of boring.

  • A front-row seat in the European startup ecosystem. Weekly exposure to leading founders and operators through internal and external events (Lunch & Learns, hackathons, community gatherings). Check out all upcoming and past events here: https://luma.com/tacto

  • You'll build something that lasts and that matters. You'll help build the company that keeps European industry competitive for the long term.

Interview Process

  1. Intro call with our Talent team

  2. Deep dive with Head of Customer Experience

  3. Onsite case study and discussion on future of FDEs

Our Background

Tacto is building the intelligence layer that connects AI to the physical world of manufacturing, starting with procurement. AI is transforming every industry, but it stops at the factory gate. The knowledge that holds manufacturing together - part costs, suppliers, materials - is scattered across systems and people. Over 50% of a product's cost originates from suppliers, making procurement the single largest cost lever in manufacturing and the missing connection between the digital and the physical world. Yet it still runs on Excel and legacy systems. We're changing that with our Procurement Intelligence Platform, trusted by hundreds of companies running billions of Euros of material.

Based in Munich, we are 100+ passionate builders who are in-office, with high expectations, fast growth, and a lot of fun. We are supported by >€50m from Sequoia, Index, and Europe's leading tech entrepreneurs and industry veterans.

Why It Matters

Manufacturing forms Europe's economic backbone, driving a fourth of Europe's GDP and providing over 30% of jobs. These hidden champions and global market leaders manufacture the physical world around us, from the machines that build our cities to the medical devices that save lives.

But the world is changing. The US dominates the digital world of bits. China is scaling the world of atoms, manufacturing at unprecedented speed and scale. Geopolitics are more uncertain than ever. Europe's strength lies in its deep industrial knowledge through generations of engineering. Manufacturing worldwide runs on European machines and software. But that heritage is only an advantage if we leverage it in the age of AI.

Tacto builds the AI that connects Atoms and Bits, empowering our Industrial Base to Stay Stronger and building a lighthouse for European tech.

What We Offer

The people at Tacto are passionate about building the organization, growing themselves, and our product while having fun and being real. We have high expectations, great talent density, and a culture where your ambition, performance, and agency are what count - not where you come from or how big your ego is. You'll grow at the forefront of AI, have real ownership and impact, and be surrounded by the best people in their field who challenge you and make you better every day. That is demanding and rewarding, but that's where we thrive. Besides that you have:

  • Money: Competitive salary & equity in the company with real upside, so you are invested in our success

  • Workplace: A vibrant in-office culture (> 4 days/week) in a beautiful office in central Munich

  • Development: A development budget and regular exposure to exceptional people, e.g., Lunch & Learns, peer mentoring, external speakers

  • Time off: 26 + 4 vacation days per year (4 fixed “company rest days”) as well as regular off-sites and team events

  • Health: Wellpass membership, of course, a fruit basket (!), and access to Jobrad, for your health

  • Family & Social Security: Voluntary pension contribution, voluntary KITA subsidy for your children

title: Senior Test Engineer - M/F/D
description:
About Navflex

At Navflex, we're pioneering the future of logistics automation through cutting-edge AI and

robotics. Our autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) are transforming the way goods are loaded

and unloaded, enabling plug-and-play solutions that streamline operations and enhance

efficiency across the global supply chain for some of the world’s most demanding warehouse

Environments. Our international, cross‑disciplinary team in the EU and USA pairs robust mechatronics with cutting‑edge navigation and perception to deliver safe, reliable autonomy in real‑world warehouses and yards. Join us in shaping the future of intelligent logistics.

 

What makes us different

  • We bring hardware and AI into production, not just prototypes

  • We work directly with real warehouse operations and customer environments

  • We build systems that must be safe, reliable, and economically viable

 

What you can expect at the Munich Team

You will join a highly skilled, hands-on engineering team working at the intersection of robotics, product development, and real-world deployment, with direct impact on systems used by global customers.

 

What We Offer

  • The opportunity to work on robotics systems that are already used in real-world environments

  • A role where you can actively shape systems and see the impact of your work

  • A collaborative, international team with diverse backgrounds and perspectives

  • Plenty of room for personal and professional growth as we continue to scale

  • Challenging work alongside experienced engineers who are passionate about what they do

  • A culture that values ownership, learning, and continuous improvement

  • Competitive compensation

The Role

You will own system-level validation of Navflex’s autonomous forklift AMR—by continuously testing new software on real vehicles, stress-testing the system against the operational domain, and building automated test infrastructure that closes the gap between lab results and field performance.

This is not a “ticket-only QA” role. You will reproduce issues, analyze logs and data, and drive investigations far enough to pinpoint the most likely subsystem (perception, localization, planning, controls, HW interface, fleet services) and the fastest path to root cause and fix.

 

Success Measures - Success in this role will be measured by:

  • Regressions are caught early and software is released with evidence-based readiness.

  • Test coverage expands across the operational design domain (ODD), including edge cases and failure modes.

  • Field issues become reproducible in lab/replay/HIL with clear fault isolation and actionable engineering feedback.

  • A scalable automation framework exists (SIL/HIL + log replay + on-robot tests) with dashboards and automated reporting.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Own scenario-based validation across the operational domain

    • Define and maintain an Operational Design Domain (ODD) and scenario library that reflects real warehouse and trailer-loading workflows (normal operation, edge cases, abuse cases).

    • Translate requirements and known risks into testable acceptance criteria, pass/fail metrics, and release gates.

    • Design and execute functional, regression, performance, reliability, and safety validation plans at the system level.

    • Plan long-duration stability/endurance campaigns and track reliability trends over time.

  • Continuously test software on real vehicles (lab + field)

    • Own day-to-day test execution on a vehicle fleet: smoke tests, nightly/weekly regressions, and targeted experiments for new features and bug fixes.

    • Run structured test sessions that intentionally challenge autonomy behavior in a safe, controlled way (tight spaces, occlusions, pallet variability, trailer geometry, degraded sensors, etc.).

    • Support pilots and customer transitions; ensure evidence-based sign-off for rollout and ramp.

  • Debug, reproduce, and isolate issues using logs and data

    • Reproduce failures using on-robot tests, log replay, simulation, and HIL as appropriate.

    • Analyze logs/traces and recorded datasets (e.g., ROS bag files, telemetry, event logs) to identify failure signatures and likely root causes.

    • Create high-signal bug reports with minimal repro steps, expected vs. actual behavior, and supporting evidence (plots, log snippets, metrics).

    • Partner with engineers to drive issues to closure and prevent regressions.

  • Build automated test infrastructure (SIL/HIL + reporting)

    • Develop automated test scripts that run against simulation and log replay, and extend them to execute on physical robots where feasible.

    • Design and implement Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) capabilities to validate critical interfaces and autonomy behavior without always needing a full vehicle-in-the-loop setup.

    • Integrate automated tests into CI/CD (per-PR, nightly, and release-candidate runs).

    • Build tooling to compare expected vs. actual vehicle behavior from logged data; establish dashboards for coverage, pass rates, and reliability trends.

    • Automate test reporting and release readiness summaries for engineering, product, and operations stakeholders.

  • Improve test process and raise the quality bar

    • Own test request intake: guide developers to the right validation method (unit/integration/system/HIL/field) and prioritize by risk and impact.

    • Continuously refine workflows to improve coverage, safety, and confidence in every release.

    • Mentor junior engineers and contribute to best practices in testing, documentation, and safe operations around robotic hardware.

What You’ll Bring

  • Systems-level mindset and comfort reasoning about a complex robotics stack and failure modes.

  • Strong debugging discipline and hands-on comfort with physical robots in lab and field environments.

  • Clear communication and an evidence-based approach to feedback and decision-making.

  • Ownership mentality: you take responsibility for quality outcomes, not just test execution.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, or related field (or equivalent practical experience).

  • 5+ years in system testing, validation, integration testing, or quality engineering for complex electromechanical products (robotics, autonomous systems, vehicles, industrial automation, or similar).

  • Python proficiency for test automation and data analysis; ability to read and navigate C++ codebases strongly preferred.

  • Strong Linux proficiency and experience with Git-based workflows.

  • Experience designing structured test plans and executing them with clear pass/fail criteria and documentation.

  • Professional fluency in English.

  • Willingness to travel up to 20% of the time.

Preferred, But Not Required

  • Experience testing AMRs/AGVs, autonomous forklifts, or other mobile robots in production environments.

  • Experience with ROS or ROS 2 (introspection tooling, bagging/replay, launch/test utilities).

  • Experience with simulation or digital twin environments (e.g., Gazebo, Isaac Sim, Webots, Unity) and sim-to-real validation practices.

  • Experience with HIL/SIL test setups, fault injection, and long-duration stability testing.

  • Experience validating API contracts and distributed systems that interface with robot fleets (fleet manager, telemetry pipeline, integrations).

  • Familiarity with safety standards relevant to driverless industrial trucks (e.g., ISO 3691-4) and safe testing practices around heavy equipment.

  • Experience with test management/bug tracking tools (e.g., ClickUp, TestRail) and building metrics dashboards.

  • German language proficiency.

Work Environment & Safety

This role involves hands-on work around industrial robotic equipment. You must be able to follow safe operating procedures, work in warehouse environments (noise, dust, temperature variation), and support occasional after-hours or weekend test windows when needed for deployments.
